Overview

San Salvador as a Business Centre

San Salvador is the capital of El Salvador and the core of a metropolitan area that Spain's diplomatic information office estimates at about 2.3 to 2.4 million people, within a department of roughly 2 million. Following the municipal reorganisation that took effect in May 2024, the historic city is a district of the San Salvador Centro municipality; the 2024 census counted 330,543 residents in the district. The economy is dollarised, and the capital concentrates the country's banks, insurers, professional services, call centres, commerce, construction and public administration. Remittances, equal to about a quarter of national output, finance much consumption and property investment around the city.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to San Salvador because almost every significant Salvadoran company, bank and public body is managed from the capital. Foreign investors, suppliers and lenders entering the market need to know who owns and controls local partners, particularly as reforms to the business, financial and digital-asset environment have attracted new entrants. Real estate in and around the capital is a common store of value, often held through companies. Public contracts and the procurement exchange raise integrity questions. In disputes, creditors and litigants rely on the national registry, which is centralised in San Salvador, to trace companies, property and mortgages.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to San Salvador

01

Local partner and distributor diligence

Foreign companies entering El Salvador typically appoint distributors, agents or joint venture partners based in San Salvador. We research Registro de Comercio filings, directors, related companies, litigation and Spanish-language media to establish who controls a partner, whether public officials are connected and whether prior disputes or allegations exist.

02

Real estate and asset tracing

Property in the capital and nearby districts is frequently held through companies or by family members. Working with local professionals, we search the property registry and cadastre administered by the Centro Nacional de Registros to identify holdings, mortgages and transfers, supporting creditors, litigants and lenders before enforcement or security is taken.

03

Financial and digital asset counterparties

Changes to El Salvador's financial and digital asset framework have brought new exchanges, fintech firms and investors to San Salvador. We examine ownership, licensing claims, regulatory notices, principals' backgrounds and litigation, helping clients separate established operators from entities whose claims or controllers cannot be verified.

04

Public procurement integrity reviews

Ministries, autonomous institutions and municipal bodies based in the capital award significant contracts. We research bidders' shareholders and administrators, links to officials, Court of Accounts findings and press coverage to help lenders, multilateral partners and competing bidders assess conflicts of interest and connected-party risk.

05

Remittance-funded investment and fraud

Salvadorans abroad, including many in the United States, invest remittance savings in property and businesses around San Salvador and are sometimes targeted by fraud. We help counsel and clients trace companies, property and individuals involved, and document the record for civil claims or criminal complaints in El Salvador or the United States.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in San Salvador

Courts in San Salvador

The Supreme Court of Justice, including its Constitutional Chamber, sits in San Salvador, as do second-instance chambers and first-instance courts for the capital. Commercial matters are governed by the Commercial Code and the Code of Civil and Commercial Procedure and are heard by specialised mercantile courts, which handle company, banking and contract disputes. Court files are not generally searchable online, so litigation research often relies on counsel and local professionals reviewing records at the courts.

Centro Nacional de Registros

The Centro Nacional de Registros was created by Executive Decree No. 62 of December 1994 and is headquartered in the San Salvador area. It absorbed the property and mortgage registry, which dates from 1881, the Commercial Registry founded in July 1973, the social housing registry and the national geographic institute, and later intellectual property. Property registration uses a parcel-based folio real system linking legal and cadastral data. Property offices are organised by department, with San Salvador's office covering the capital.

Arbitration and mediation

Private arbitration in El Salvador operates under 2002 legislation that permits institutional arbitration centres. The main centre is the Mediation and Arbitration Centre of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of El Salvador, based in San Salvador, which administers commercial disputes between local and foreign parties. A 2009 amendment allows certain arbitral decisions to be appealed to the courts, which counsel should consider when drafting dispute clauses.

Regulators and oversight bodies

National institutions relevant to investigations are concentrated in San Salvador, including the Attorney General's Office and its Financial Investigation Unit, the Court of Accounts, which audits public bodies, and financial sector supervisors. The local securities exchange is also based in the capital. Their published decisions, audit reports and notices are useful sources for counterparty research, although access to some procurement information is limited.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in San Salvador

TDSC has no office in San Salvador and works on San Salvador matters from its Nashville headquarters. We begin by defining the decision, such as appointing a distributor, lending against property, entering a financial partnership or recovering a debt, and agree with Salvadoran counsel which records may lawfully be obtained and how personal data will be handled under current Salvadoran rules. Research uses Centro Nacional de Registros commercial and property records, court information obtained through counsel, regulatory and audit publications and Spanish-language media. Registry certifications, court file reviews and discreet enquiries in the city are carried out by qualified local professionals we coordinate. Reports separate certified registry facts from reputational information.

TDSC has no office in San Salvador. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

San Salvador: Frequently Asked Questions

Can you search the property registry in San Salvador?

Yes, through qualified local professionals. Property and mortgage records are kept by the Centro Nacional de Registros, organised by department, with records linked to the cadastre in a parcel-based system. We use searches to identify holdings, mortgages and transfers connected to a person or company, and Salvadoran counsel advises on title and enforcement.

How do you check a company registered in San Salvador?

We start with the Registro de Comercio at the Centro Nacional de Registros, which holds incorporation deeds, appointments of administrators and amendments, and certifications can be ordered. We then add litigation, regulatory and media research. We have not confirmed a public beneficial ownership register, so control is assessed from the available records.

Where are commercial disputes heard?

Commercial disputes in the capital are heard by specialised mercantile courts under the Commercial Code and the Code of Civil and Commercial Procedure, with appeals to second-instance chambers and the Supreme Court of Justice in San Salvador. Parties may also arbitrate, commonly through the Chamber of Commerce and Industry's Mediation and Arbitration Centre.

Can you help Salvadorans in the US who were defrauded at home?

We can support their counsel by tracing the companies, property and individuals involved in San Salvador through registry and open-source research, and by documenting findings for civil or criminal proceedings. We coordinate local professionals for work in El Salvador. Legal advice on remedies must come from Salvadoran or US counsel.

Does TDSC have investigators in El Salvador?

No. TDSC is headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office or staff in El Salvador. Where a matter requires on-the-ground work in San Salvador, we coordinate qualified local professionals and rely on Salvadoran counsel to confirm what may lawfully be done before work begins.
